## Jet tagging {: #jet-tagging }

<div class="table-wrap"><table class="catalogue-table catalogue-entries"><thead><tr><th>Dataset</th><th>Content</th><th>Simulation</th><th>Size</th><th>Year</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr class="row" id="top-tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="top-tagging-detail">Top Tagging Reference Dataset</button></td><td>Top vs QCD jets</td><td>Delphes (ATLAS)</td><td>2 M jets</td><td>2019</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="top-tagging-detail"><td colspan="5">

Hadronic top-quark jets against QCD jets at 14 TeV, the common benchmark of the top-tagger comparison.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Pythia 8, Delphes (ATLAS card)</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Jet-Tagging Architectures: <a href="jet-tagging.md#particlenet">ParticleNet</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#jedi-net">JEDI-net</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#point-cloud-transformer">Point Cloud Transformer</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#particle-transformer">Particle Transformer (ParT)</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#lorentz-group-network">Lorentz Group Network</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#lorentznet">LorentzNet</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#pelican">PELICAN</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#l-gatr">L-GATr</a></p><p class="row-uses">Used in Anomaly Detection: <a href="anomaly-detection.md#normalized-autoencoder">Normalized autoencoder</a></p><p class="row-uses">Used in Foundation Models: <a href="foundation-models.md#contrastive-at-scale">Contrastive pre-training at scale</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#hep-jepa">HEP-JEPA</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearned">OmniLearned</a></p>

- **Events:** Pythia 8 at $\sqrt{s} = 14$ TeV, without multiple parton
  interactions or pile-up.
- **Jets:** anti-$k_T$, $R = 0.8$, from Delphes particle-flow objects;
  $550 < p_T < 650$ GeV, $|\eta| < 2$. Top jets are matched to a top
  quark and all its decay partons within $\Delta R = 0.8$.
- **Content:** four-momenta of the 200 leading constituents,
  zero-padded, and the truth top four-momentum.
- **Splits:** 1.2 M training, 0.4 M validation and 0.4 M test jets.
- **Note:** the best taggers of the comparison reach an AUC of about
  0.98, so newer architectures differ little on this dataset.

<tr class="row" id="quark-gluon"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="quark-gluon-detail">Quark and gluon jets</button></td><td>Quark vs gluon jets</td><td>Generator level</td><td>2 M jets per version</td><td>2019</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="quark-gluon-detail"><td colspan="5">

Quark and gluon jets from $Z$+jet events at 14 TeV, at generator level, in Pythia 8 and Herwig 7 versions.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Pythia 8 or Herwig 7.1.4, generator level</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Jet-Tagging Architectures: <a href="jet-tagging.md#efn-pfn">Energy and Particle Flow Networks</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#particlenet">ParticleNet</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#point-cloud-transformer">Point Cloud Transformer</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#particle-transformer">Particle Transformer (ParT)</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#lorentznet">LorentzNet</a></p><p class="row-uses">Used in Foundation Models: <a href="foundation-models.md#hep-jepa">HEP-JEPA</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearned">OmniLearned</a></p>

- **Events:** quarks from $qg \to Z(\to \nu\bar\nu)q$, gluons from
  $q\bar q \to Z(\to \nu\bar\nu)g$; no detector simulation.
- **Jets:** anti-$k_T$, $R = 0.4$; $500 < p_T < 550$ GeV,
  $|y| < 1.7$.
- **Content:** 20 files of 100,000 jets each, half quarks and half
  gluons, as per-particle arrays; one version without charm and
  bottom quarks in the hard process (the one used in the paper) and
  one with them.

<p class="row-links"><a href="papers.md#komiske-2018cqr">Paper</a><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05165">arXiv</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3164691">Data (Pythia)</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3066475">Data (Herwig)</a><button type="button" class="cite-button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" data-cite="Komiske:2018cqr data:quark-gluon-pythia data:quark-gluon-herwig" data-file="quark-gluon">Cite</button><a class="cited-by" href="https://inspirehep.net/literature?q=refersto%3Arecid%3A1698236">Cited by</a></p>

<tr class="row" id="jetclass"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="jetclass-detail">JetClass</button></td><td>Boosted jets in 10 classes</td><td>Delphes (CMS)</td><td>125 M jets</td><td>2022</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="jetclass-detail"><td colspan="5">

125 M jets in ten classes of boosted-jet signatures, released with the Particle Transformer.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia, Delphes (CMS card)</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Jet-Tagging Architectures: <a href="jet-tagging.md#particle-transformer">Particle Transformer (ParT)</a></p><p class="row-uses">Used in Foundation Models: <a href="foundation-models.md#contrastive-at-scale">Contrastive pre-training at scale</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#masked-particle-modelling">Masked particle modelling</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#masked-particle-modelling-without-tokens">Masked particle modelling without tokens</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#hep-jepa">HEP-JEPA</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#omnijet-alpha">OmniJet-α</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearn">OmniLearn</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearned">OmniLearned</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#analysis-fine-tuning">Fine-tuning for analysis</a></p>

- **Classes:** $q/g$ background; $H \to b\bar b$, $H \to c\bar c$,
  $H \to gg$, $H \to 4q$, $H \to \ell\nu qq'$, $Z \to q\bar q$,
  $W \to qq'$, $t \to bqq'$, $t \to b\ell\nu$.
- **Events:** multiple parton interactions included, no pile-up;
  Delphes CMS card with track impact parameters smeared to the CMS
  tracker resolution.
- **Jets:** anti-$k_T$, $R = 0.8$; $500 < p_T < 1000$ GeV,
  $|\eta| < 2$; signal jets contain all decay products of the
  initial particle.
- **Splits:** 100 M training, 5 M validation and 20 M test jets.
- **Tools:** loaders and the Particle Transformer at
  <https://github.com/jet-universe/particle_transformer>.

<p class="row-links"><a href="papers.md#qu-2022mxj">Paper</a><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03772">arXiv</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6619768">Data</a><button type="button" class="cite-button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" data-cite="Qu:2022mxj data:jetclass" data-file="jetclass">Cite</button><a class="cited-by" href="https://inspirehep.net/literature?q=refersto%3Arecid%3A2029602">Cited by</a></p>

<tr class="row" id="jetclass-ii"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="jetclass-ii-detail">JetClass-II</button></td><td>Boosted jets in 188 classes</td><td>Delphes (CMS), pile-up</td><td></td><td>2024</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="jetclass-ii-detail"><td colspan="5">

Jets in 188 finely divided classes, made to pre-train the Sophon model for resonance searches.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: JetClass workflow with pile-up</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Foundation Models: <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearned">OmniLearned</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#sophon">Sophon</a></p>

- **Classes:** include resonant jets with two, three or four prongs
  initiated by quarks, gluons or leptons, over a wider mass range
  than JetClass.
- **Events:** the JetClass simulation with an average pile-up of 50,
  removed by per-particle pile-up identification.
- **Format:** Parquet files on Hugging Face.

<tr class="row" id="hls4ml-jets"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="hls4ml-jets-detail">hls4ml LHC jets</button></td><td>q, g, W, Z and top jets</td><td>Pythia 8</td><td>5 classes</td><td>2020</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="hls4ml-jets-detail"><td colspan="5">

Light-quark, gluon, $W$, $Z$ and top jets near 1 TeV, prepared for studies of neural-network inference on FPGAs.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia 8, 13 TeV</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Jet-Tagging Architectures: <a href="jet-tagging.md#jedi-net">JEDI-net</a>, <a href="jet-tagging.md#point-cloud-transformer">Point Cloud Transformer</a></p>

- **Content:** high-level jet features (Duarte et al.), jet images
  and lists of up to 150 constituents (Moreno et al.).
- **Events:** partons generated in a narrow $p_T$ window centred at
  1 TeV, showered with Pythia 8.212 (Monash 2013 tune).

<p class="row-links"><a href="papers.md#duarte-2018ite">Paper</a><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06913">arXiv</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3602260">Data</a><button type="button" class="cite-button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" data-cite="Duarte:2018ite Moreno:2019bmu data:hls4ml-jets" data-file="hls4ml-jets">Cite</button><a class="cited-by" href="https://inspirehep.net/literature?q=refersto%3Arecid%3A1668914">Cited by</a></p>

<tr class="row" id="atlas-top-tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="atlas-top-tagging-detail">ATLAS top tagging</button></td><td>Top vs QCD jets, with systematics</td><td>Full sim (ATLAS)</td><td>103 M jets</td><td>2024</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="atlas-top-tagging-detail"><td colspan="5">

Top-quark and QCD jets in full ATLAS simulation, with samples that vary one systematic effect at a time.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Full ATLAS simulation</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Foundation Models: <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearn">OmniLearn</a>, <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearned">OmniLearned</a></p>

- **Nominal:** 92.8 M training and 10.3 M test jets, equal numbers of
  top jets and light-quark or gluon jets.
- **Variations:** calorimeter-cluster energy scale, resolution and
  position; track efficiency, fake rate and bias; top jets from
  Pythia and from Herwig; background jets with cluster and with
  string hadronisation. For evaluation, not training.
- **Rule:** each jet's contribution to the loss must be multiplied by
  its training weight.
- **Superseded:** the 2022 record (42 M training, 2.5 M test jets).

<p class="row-links"><a href="papers.md#atlas-2024rua">Paper</a><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20127">arXiv</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.7483/OPENDATA.ATLAS.SOAY.LABE">Data</a><button type="button" class="cite-button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" data-cite="ATLAS:2024rua data:atlas-top-tagging" data-file="atlas-top-tagging">Cite</button><a class="cited-by" href="https://inspirehep.net/literature?q=refersto%3Arecid%3A2811690">Cited by</a></p>

<tr class="row-detail" id="cms-hbb-detail"><td colspan="5">

Jets from $H \to b\bar b$ decays against QCD jets in full CMS simulation, with track and secondary-vertex features.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Full CMS simulation, 13 TeV</p>

- **Jets:** anti-$k_T$, $R = 0.8$, from particle-flow candidates,
  with charged-hadron subtraction of pile-up.
- **Content:** jet features, charged-track features, and the
  secondary vertices within $\Delta R < 0.8$ of the jet axis.

<tr class="row" id="jet-images"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="jet-images-detail">\(W\) and QCD jet images</button></td><td>W vs QCD jet images</td><td>Pythia 8, pixelated</td><td>0.87 M images</td><td>2017</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="jet-images-detail"><td colspan="5">

25 × 25 calorimeter-style images of $W$-boson and QCD jets, released with the LAGAN generative model.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Pythia 8.219, 14 TeV</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Generative Models: <a href="generative-models.md#lagan">LAGAN</a></p>

- **Jets:** anti-$k_T$, $R = 1.0$; $250 < p_T < 300$ GeV,
  $60 < m < 100$ GeV.
- **Images:** a $0.1 \times 0.1$ grid in $\eta$ and $\phi$ over
  $[-1.25, 1.25]^2$, pixel intensity $p_T$, preprocessed as in the
  jet-images paper.
- **Content:** images with jet mass, $p_T$ and $n$-subjettiness
  ratios.

<tr class="row" id="jetnet"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="jetnet-detail">JetNet</button></td><td>g, q, t, W, Z particle clouds</td><td>Simplified detector</td><td>0.88 M jets</td><td>2021</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="jetnet-detail"><td colspan="5">

Gluon, light-quark, top, $W$ and $Z$ jets near 1 TeV as particle clouds, for generative models of jets.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: 13 TeV, simplified detector</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Generative Models: <a href="generative-models.md#mpgan">MPGAN</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#epic-gan">EPiC-GAN</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#pc-jedi">PC-JeDi</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#fast-point-cloud-diffusion">Fast point cloud diffusion</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#epic-jedi-fm">EPiC-JeDi and EPiC-FM</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#mean-field-attention-gan">Mean-field attention GAN</a></p>

- **Particles:** up to 30 (JetNet) or 150 (JetNet150) per jet, with
  $\eta$, $\phi$ and $p_T$ relative to the jet and a mask.
- **Jets:** $p_T$, $\eta$, mass and multiplicity; between 170,679
  and 177,945 jets per class.
- **Tools:** the `jetnet` package loads both and implements the
  evaluation metrics, among them the Fréchet and kernel physics
  distances.

<tr class="row-detail" id="calochallenge-detail"><td colspan="5">

Geant4 calorimeter showers in three datasets of increasing granularity, from the Fast Calorimeter Simulation Challenge.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Geant4 (ATLAS for Dataset 1)</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Generative Models: <a href="generative-models.md#icaloflow">iCaloFlow</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#caloscore">CaloScore</a>, <a href="generative-models.md#calodiffusion">CaloDiffusion</a></p>

- **Dataset 1:** ATLAS Geant4 showers of photons and charged pions
  at $0.2 < \eta < 0.25$, 15 energies from 256 MeV to 4 TeV in powers
  of two.
- **Datasets 2 and 3:** electron showers, energies log-uniform in
  1 GeV to 1 TeV, in 45 silicon–tungsten layers; 6,480 voxels
  ($9 \times 16$ per layer) and 40,500 voxels ($18 \times 50$ per
  layer, produced with the Par04 Geant4 example).
- **Splits:** separate files for training and for evaluation.
- **Results:** the paper compares 31 submissions.

## Anomaly detection {: #anomaly-detection }

<div class="table-wrap"><table class="catalogue-table catalogue-entries"><thead><tr><th>Dataset</th><th>Content</th><th>Simulation</th><th>Size</th><th>Year</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr class="row" id="lhc-olympics"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="lhc-olympics-detail">LHC Olympics 2020</button></td><td>Dijets with a hidden resonance</td><td>Delphes</td><td>5.1 M events</td><td>2019</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="lhc-olympics-detail"><td colspan="5">

Dijet events with a hidden $W' \to XY$ resonance, for resonant anomaly detection.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Pythia 8, Delphes 3.4.1</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Anomaly Detection: <a href="anomaly-detection.md#tag-n-train">Tag N&#x27; Train</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#boosted-decision-trees">Boosted decision trees</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#anode">ANODE</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#r-anode">R-ANODE</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#salad">SALAD</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#cathode">CATHODE</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#curtains">CURTAINs</a>, <a href="anomaly-detection.md#feta">FETA</a></p><p class="row-uses">Used in Foundation Models: <a href="foundation-models.md#omnilearn">OmniLearn</a></p>

- **R&D set:** 1 M QCD dijet events and 100,000 $W' \to XY$,
  $X \to jj$, $Y \to jj$ events with masses 3.5 TeV, 500 GeV and
  100 GeV, with a truth bit; no pile-up or multiple parton
  interactions.
- **Black boxes:** three samples of 1 M events and a 1 M background
  sample; solutions for black boxes 1 and 3, and the Delphes cards
  and Pythia settings, were added after the challenge.
- **Content:** reconstructed particles as massless
  $(p_T, \eta, \phi)$, zero-padded to 700 particles.
- **Caution:** the R&D set requires a large-radius ($R = 1$) jet with
  $p_T > 1.3$ TeV, the black boxes $p_T > 1.2$ TeV.

<p class="row-links"><a href="papers.md#kasieczka-2021xcg">Paper</a><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.08320">arXiv</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2629073">R&amp;D set</a><a href="https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4536624">Black boxes</a><button type="button" class="cite-button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" data-cite="Kasieczka:2021xcg data:lhc-olympics-rnd data:lhc-olympics-black-boxes" data-file="lhc-olympics">Cite</button><a class="cited-by" href="https://inspirehep.net/literature?q=refersto%3Arecid%3A1842125">Cited by</a></p>

<tr class="row" id="dark-machines"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="dark-machines-detail">Dark Machines</button></td><td>SM events and 40+ signals</td><td>Delphes (ATLAS)</td><td>over 10⁹ events</td><td>2020</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="dark-machines-detail"><td colspan="5">

Over a billion Standard Model events in four channels, with more than 40 signals, for unsupervised new-physics searches.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia 8, Delphes (ATLAS card)</p>

- **Content:** reconstructed objects with $E$, $p_T$, $\eta$,
  $\phi$, and the missing transverse momentum, in CSV files.
- **Records:** the full generation, a labelled hackathon sample, and
  an unlabelled secret sample kept blinded for future comparisons.

<tr class="row-detail" id="adc2021-detail"><td colspan="5">

Lepton-filtered Standard Model events at 13 TeV, for unsupervised new-physics detection at the first trigger level.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Delphes 3.3.2 (CMS Phase-2 card)</p>

- **Filter:** an electron or muon with $p_T > 23$ GeV, chosen to keep
  the simulation tractable; the detector resolution is not degraded
  to that of trigger reconstruction.
- **Records:** signal samples and a blinded test set are listed at
  <https://mpp-hep.github.io/ADC2021/>.

<tr class="row-detail" id="higgs-susy-detail"><td colspan="5">

Signal and background events as tabular features, also used outside physics as tabular benchmarks.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: MadGraph 5, Pythia, Delphes, 8 TeV</p>

- **Sizes:** 11 M events (HIGGS), 5 M events (SUSY).
- **HIGGS:** heavy-Higgs signal in the $\ell\nu jjb\bar b$ final state
  against $t\bar t$; 21 low-level features and 7 invariant masses.
- **SUSY:** chargino-pair signal; 8 low-level and 10 derived
  features.
- **Finding:** deep networks given only the low-level features
  outperform shallow networks given the derived ones.

- **Competition:** held at NeurIPS 2024.

<tr class="row-detail" id="omnifold-detail"><td colspan="5">

$Z$+jet events from Herwig and Pythia at particle and detector level, for unfolding.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Herwig 7.1.5, Pythia 8.243, Delphes 3.4.2 (CMS card)</p>

<p class="row-uses">Used in Simulation-Based Inference: <a href="simulation-based-inference.md#omnifold">OmniFold</a></p>

- **Events:** 14 TeV, $Z$ with $p_T > 150$ GeV; Herwig default tune
  and Pythia A14 tune with two of its variations.
- **Jets:** anti-$k_T$, $R = 0.4$, at particle and detector level, so
  that one generator can stand in for data and another for
  simulation.

<tr class="row-detail" id="mlpf-clic-detail"><td colspan="5">

Full simulation of $e^+e^-$ collisions at 380 GeV in the CLIC detector, for particle-flow reconstruction.

<p class="row-facts">Simulation: Full CLIC simulation (Key4hep)</p>

- **Processes:** $t\bar t$, $Z^* \to q\bar q$, $ZH$ with
  $H \to \tau\tau$, hadronic $WW$, $t\bar t$ with overlaid
  background, and single-particle samples.
- **Content:** EDM4hep files with generator particles, tracks,
  calorimeter hits and Pandora particle-flow candidates.

## See also {: #see-also }

- The [Living Review of Machine Learning for Particle Physics](papers.md#feickert-2021ajf)
  lists the papers of the field by topic, with a section on datasets:
  <https://iml-wg.github.io/HEPML-LivingReview/>.
- The [OmniLearned](papers.md#bhimji-2025isp) foundation model pre-trains on
  about a billion jets pooled from JetClass, the ATLAS top-tagging data and
  other public samples.
- The experiments' own releases are searchable on the CERN Open Data Portal:
  <https://opendata.cern.ch/>.
